original_card.question: Can the 64-per-call centre path (eight rank-8 COPY/ERASE totals through the private temporary) be shared across calls or shrunk?
methods: Derive a fully charged favorable relaxation for sharing one centre path across k calls, including restoration, hosting and precision.
Prove a lower bound on copied information per call for the selected decoder contract.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Show the changed centre charge and copy profile per call with every added restoration or hosting cost charged, and its ceiling via ceiling.ceiling(centre=...). A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write the per-call centre charge and copy children for sharing across k = 2 calls, charge the sharing overhead, and screen it; stop this route if even the ideal sharing gains under 10%. Ideal budgets: free 2.80x, shared by two 1.90x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: The centre path consumes 64 of about 99.6 unpaid coordinates per call, i.e. about 64% of the raw deficit.
allowed_variations: One sharing pattern across a fixed number of calls.
One reduced copied-total contract for the existing decoder.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Removing copies without a replacement contract for the decoder's copied totals.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: Audit the distance-2 triangle-count lower bound used by the centre-path block-floor screen, with an exact C4-free incidence example at |B| = 13.
scope_change_reason: The active centre-sharing package lists labelled incidence at |B| = 13 as an open next step. Before extending its degree-capacity screen, I checked the triangle lower-bound expression used there and found an exact 13-by-13 C4-free incidence example for which the expression exceeds the true count. This narrows the work to an exact audit of that proof step; it does not decide the labelled |B| = 13 problem.
bottleneck_link: The centre path remains the selected local bottleneck, but the next block-size screen needs a valid six-cycle lower bound before its degree-only rejection can support a labelled obstruction.
stop_rule: Stop after the exact counterexample and identity are independently reproducible. Do not infer a braid-capacity-feasible incidence graph, reject all |B| = 13 graphs, extend the |B| <= 12 theorem, or change any kappa bound from this audit.
evidence: For B = D = Z/13 with D_j adjacent to B_{j}, B_{j+1}, B_{j+3}, every vertex has degree 3 and the incidence graph is C4-free. The distance-2 graph has 39 triangles, including 13 incidence claws and 26 six-cycles. The audited expression gives 52 triangles and a claimed 39-cycle lower bound because it omits the 13 triangles of the complement graph. This refutes that lower-bound step for the stated graph class; the example itself exceeds the degree-3 braid-cycle capacity and is not a feasible braid-labelled witness.
author: OpenAI Codex
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance in selecting the proof audit, deriving the exact finite counterexample, and implementing the verifier. No independent human or formal-kernel review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can a valid degree-profile lower bound, or an exact labelled search, settle the m = 13 incidence case under the actual braid-edge and dependent-triple constraints?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The |B| = 13 case is the first unresolved block size in the predecessor's two-stage block-floor question, and the audited degree screen cannot be extended with the invalid triangle proxy.
open_questions.first_step: Derive a lower bound that includes the complement-triangle term, then compare it against the per-vertex braid capacities; if it is too weak, encode the pinned labelled incidence constraints directly.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package supplies neither a corrected uniform bound nor a satisfying or unsatisfiable labelled certificate for m = 13.
